answer: Operator liability escrow makes each issuer post one shared deposit covering all wallets it registers. A misbehavior pulse from any wallet is matched to issuance logs; a cluster match freezes the issuer key. Once overlap crosses the detection ledge, the whole deposit is clawed back, so the operator—not the wallet—pays. An attacker must fund the full deposit and abandon the fable of cheap identities, costing the deposit divided by batch size plus lost issuance rights.
